k.rabb.s: Who is my Lord, and why did He create me?
k.rabb.who.a: My Lord is Allah. He created me and everything, and He gives me all the good things I have.
k.rabb.why.a: He created us to worship Him alone, and not to worship anything else with Him.
k.rabb.ibada.a: Everything Allah loves of words and deeds, such as prayer, calling on Him, being good to parents, and telling the truth.
k.rabb.know.q: How do you know your Lord?
k.rabb.know.a: I know Him through what He created and His signs: night and day, the sun and the moon, the sky and the earth.
k.rabb.where.a: Allah is above the heavens, over His Throne. He sees us, hears us and knows everything, wherever we are.
k.rabb.like.q: Is anything in creation like Allah?
k.rabb.like.a: No. Nothing is like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
k.rabb.tawhid.a: To worship Allah alone: we call on Him alone, pray to Him alone, and rely on Him alone.
k.rabb.shirk.a: Shirk: worshipping anything else along with Allah. Only Allah deserves to be worshipped.
k.rabb.z1.q: Who created us and provides for us?
k.rabb.z4.q: Does Allah see and hear us?
k.deen.what.a: My religion is Islam: I worship Allah alone, I obey Him, and I worship nothing else with Him.
k.deen.arkan.q: How many pillars does Islam have?
k.deen.arkan.l:
To testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah
To pray the five daily prayers
To give zakah
To fast in Ramadan
To make the pilgrimage (Hajj) to the House of Allah, for those who are able
k.deen.lailaha.q: What does «لا إله إلا الله» (lā ilāha illa-llāh) mean?
k.deen.lailaha.a: No one has the right to be worshipped except Allah. So we worship only Allah.
k.deen.rasul.q: What does «محمد رسول الله» (Muḥammadun rasūlu-llāh) mean?
k.deen.rasul.a: Allah sent him to all people. So we believe him, obey him, and follow his way (the Sunnah).
k.deen.salah.q: How many prayers do we pray each day and night?
k.deen.salah.a: Five prayers: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.
k.deen.sawm.a: We fast the month of Ramadan, from dawn until sunset.
k.deen.zakah.a: Zakah is wealth the rich give to the poor, as Allah commanded. Hajj is visiting the House of Allah in Makkah once in a lifetime, for those who are able.
k.deen.z1.q: How many pillars does Islam have?
k.deen.z2.q: What is the first pillar of Islam?
k.deen.z3.q: In which month do we fast?
k.deen.z4.q: How many prayers are there each day and night?
k.nabi.s: Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
k.nabi.who.a: My Prophet is Muhammad, son of Abdullah ﷺ, from the tribe of Quraysh, a descendant of Ismail, son of Ibrahim, peace be upon them.
k.nabi.born.q: Where was he born, and where did he migrate to?
k.nabi.born.a: He was born in Makkah and migrated to Madinah, where he passed away ﷺ.
k.nabi.wahy.q: When did revelation come to him?
k.nabi.wahy.a: Revelation came to him when he was forty years old, in the Cave of Hira. The first verses of the Quran revealed to him were the beginning of Surah al-ʿAlaq.
k.nabi.last.q: Will any prophet come after him?
k.nabi.last.a: No. He is the last of the prophets and messengers.
k.nabi.sent.a: Allah sent him as a mercy to the worlds, to call people to worship Allah alone and to teach them what is good.
k.nabi.love.q: How do we love the Prophet ﷺ?
k.nabi.love.a: We love him more than all other people, we obey him, and we follow his Sunnah.
k.nabi.khuluq.q: What was his character like ﷺ?
k.nabi.khuluq.a: He had the best character of all people: truthful, trustworthy, merciful and generous.
k.nabi.anbiya.q: Who were the prophets before him?
k.nabi.anbiya.a: There were many prophets, among them Adam, Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses) and ʿIsa (Jesus), peace be upon them. All of them called people to worship Allah alone.
k.nabi.z1.q: What is our Prophet's name ﷺ?
k.nabi.z2.q: Where was the Prophet ﷺ born?
k.nabi.z3.q: How old was he when revelation came to him?
k.nabi.z4.q: Will a prophet come after Muhammad ﷺ?
k.nabi.z4.0: No, he is the last prophet
k.iman.six.q: How many pillars of faith (Iman) are there?
k.iman.six.l:
Allah
His angels
His books
His messengers
The Last Day
The divine decree (Qadar), its good and its bad
k.iman.malaika.a: They are a creation of Allah, made from light. They obey Him and never disobey. One of them is Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, who brought the revelation to the prophets.
k.iman.kutub.q: What are the books of Allah?
k.iman.kutub.a: Books Allah sent down to His messengers, among them the Torah, the Gospel (Injil) and the Psalms (Zabur). The last is the Quran, which Allah has protected from any change.
k.iman.rusul.a: They are human beings Allah chose to teach people His religion. The last of them is Muhammad ﷺ. We believe in all of them and love them.
k.iman.akhira.a: The Day of Resurrection: Allah will bring people back to life after death and judge their deeds. Whoever believed and did good will enter Paradise.
k.iman.qadar.q: What does it mean to believe in the divine decree (Qadar)?
k.iman.qadar.a: To believe that Allah knows everything, has written everything, and that nothing happens unless He wills it. So we thank Him for what is good and are patient with what befalls us.
k.iman.z1.q: How many pillars of faith are there?
k.iman.z2.q: What were the angels created from?
k.iman.z3.q: Which is the last of Allah's books?
k.iman.z4.2: We do not know his name
k.wudu.why.a: Because Allah commanded us to make wudu before prayer, and prayer is not valid without purification.
k.wudu.how.a: I make wudu in this order:
k.wudu.how.l:
I intend it in my heart and say: «بسم الله» (Bismillāh).
I wash my hands three times.
I rinse my mouth and nose three times.
I wash my face three times.
I wash my arms up to the elbows three times, the right and then the left.
I wipe my head once, and wipe my ears.
I wash my feet up to the ankles three times, the right and then the left.
k.wudu.after.q: What do I say after wudu?
k.wudu.breaks.a: Some things break wudu, among them: using the toilet, passing wind, and deep sleep.
k.wudu.water.a: No. I make wudu with a little water and do not waste it, because Allah does not love those who waste.
k.wudu.khala.q: What do I say when entering and leaving the toilet?
k.wudu.khala.a: I enter with my left foot and say the entering supplication. I leave with my right foot and say: «غفرانك» (Ghufrānak).
k.wudu.z1.q: What do I say at the start of wudu?
k.wudu.z2.q: How many times do I wipe my head?
k.wudu.z3.q: What is the last thing I wash in wudu?
k.salah.what.a: A great act of worship in which we stand before Allah five times every day. It is the pillar of the religion.
k.salah.count.q: How many rakʿahs (units) are in each prayer?
k.salah.count.a: Each prayer has a number of rakʿahs:
k.salah.count.l:
Fajr: two
Dhuhr: four
Asr: four
Maghrib: three
Isha: four
k.salah.age.a: The Prophet ﷺ taught that children should be told to pray when they are seven years old. And I love to pray with my father and mother from now.
k.salah.how.a: I pray as the Prophet ﷺ prayed:
k.salah.how.l:
I make wudu, wear clean clothes and face the qiblah.
I say «الله أكبر» (Allāhu akbar), then recite al-Fatihah and some more of the Quran.
I bow and say: «سبحان ربي العظيم» (Subḥāna rabbiya-l-ʿaẓīm).
I stand up and say: «سمع الله لمن حمده، ربنا ولك الحمد» (Samiʿa-llāhu liman ḥamidah, rabbanā wa laka-l-ḥamd).
I prostrate and say: «سبحان ربي الأعلى» (Subḥāna rabbiya-l-aʿlā), then I sit, then I prostrate a second time.
At the end of the prayer I recite the tashahhud, then I say the salam to my right and to my left.
k.salah.qibla.q: Which way do I face in prayer?
k.salah.qibla.a: I face the qiblah: the Kaʿbah in Makkah.
k.salah.khushu.q: How do I stand in my prayer?
k.salah.khushu.a: I stand calmly and respectfully. I do not look around or play, because I am standing before Allah.
k.salah.z1.q: How many rakʿahs is the Maghrib prayer?
k.salah.z2.q: What do I say when bowing?
k.salah.z3.q: Which way do I face in prayer?
k.salah.z4.q: How do I begin the prayer?
k.quran.s: The words of Allah that I love
k.quran.what.a: It is the speech of Allah. He sent it down to our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through Jibril, peace be upon him, to guide people to what is good.
k.quran.count.q: How many surahs are in the Quran?
k.quran.count.a: One hundred and fourteen surahs. The first is al-Fatihah and the last is an-Nas.
k.quran.adab.q: How do I read the Quran?
k.quran.adab.a: I read it in a state of purity, slowly and respectfully, and I begin by saying: «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم» (Aʿūdhu billāhi mina-sh-shayṭāni-r-rajīm).
k.quran.best.q: Who are the best of people?
k.quran.best.a: The Prophet ﷺ told us that the best of people are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
k.quran.ajr.q: What is the reward for reading the Quran?
k.quran.ajr.a: For every letter I read I get a good deed, and each good deed is multiplied by ten.
k.quran.hifz.a: I start with Surah al-Fatihah, then the short surahs: al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas.
k.quran.z1.1: The speech of the Prophet ﷺ
k.quran.z2.q: How many surahs are in the Quran?
k.quran.z3.q: What is the first surah in the Mushaf?
k.quran.z4.q: How many good deeds do I get for each letter I read?
k.akhlaq.parents.q: How do I treat my parents?
k.akhlaq.parents.a: I obey them, I am good to them, I speak to them politely, and I pray for them.
k.akhlaq.sidq.q: Why do I always tell the truth?
k.akhlaq.sidq.a: Because truthfulness leads to goodness, and goodness leads to Paradise. A Muslim does not lie.
k.akhlaq.salam.a: I say: «السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته» (As-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatu-llāhi wa barakātuh). When someone greets me, I answer: «وعليكم السلام ورحمة الله وبركاته» (Wa ʿalaykumu-s-salāmu wa raḥmatu-llāhi wa barakātuh).
k.akhlaq.food.q: What are the manners of eating?
k.akhlaq.food.a: I say «بسم الله» (Bismillāh), I eat with my right hand, I eat from what is in front of me, and I thank Allah when I finish.
k.akhlaq.sleep.q: What do I say when I go to sleep and when I wake up?
k.akhlaq.sleep.a: I lie on my right side and say the supplication of sleep, and when I wake up I praise Allah.
k.akhlaq.sneeze.q: What do I say when I sneeze?
k.akhlaq.sneeze.a: I say: «الحمد لله» (Alḥamdulillāh). My brother says to me: «يرحمك الله» (Yarḥamuka-llāh). Then I say: «يهديكم الله ويصلح بالكم» (Yahdīkumu-llāhu wa yuṣliḥu bālakum).
k.akhlaq.tongue.q: How do I guard my tongue?
k.akhlaq.tongue.a: I say what is good or stay silent. I do not swear, lie, or make fun of anyone.
k.akhlaq.rahma.q: How do I treat people and animals?
k.akhlaq.rahma.a: I love for others what I love for myself. I am kind to those younger than me, I respect my elders, and I am gentle with animals and never hurt them.
k.akhlaq.anger.q: What do I do when I get angry?
k.akhlaq.anger.a: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, I stay silent, and I hurt no one. The Prophet ﷺ advised a man: “Do not get angry.”
k.akhlaq.amana.a: To take care of what I am given, to return what I borrow, and never to take what is not mine.
k.akhlaq.z1.q: Which hand do I eat with?
k.akhlaq.z2.q: What do I say before eating?
k.akhlaq.z3.q: What do I say when I sneeze?
k.akhlaq.z4.q: Which of these does a Muslim do?
k.dhikr.dua.a: I call upon Allah alone. He hears me and answers my prayer.
k.dhikr.help.q: Whom do I ask for help?
k.dhikr.help.a: The Prophet ﷺ taught Ibn ʿAbbas when he was a boy: when you ask, ask Allah, and when you seek help, seek help from Allah.
k.dhikr.sabah.q: What do I say in the morning and the evening?
k.dhikr.sabah.a: I say the morning and evening adhkar so that Allah protects me. One of them is this, said three times:
k.dhikr.home.q: What do I say when I leave the house?
k.dhikr.home.a: I say this remembrance and put my trust in Allah:
k.dhikr.tasbih.q: Which words does Allah love most?
k.dhikr.tasbih.a: Four phrases: «سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر» (Subḥāna-llāh, wa-l-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illa-llāh, wa-llāhu akbar).
k.dhikr.tawba.q: What do I do when I make a mistake?
k.dhikr.tawba.a: I say «أستغفر الله» (Astaghfiru-llāh), I repent and do not go back to it, and I do a good deed afterwards. Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
k.dhikr.salat.q: What do I say when the Prophet ﷺ is mentioned?
k.dhikr.salat.a: I say: «صلى الله عليه وسلم» (Ṣalla-llāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam). Whoever sends blessings on him once, Allah sends blessings on that person ten times.
k.dhikr.z1.q: Whom do I call upon and ask?
k.dhikr.z2.q: What do I say when I make a mistake?
k.dhikr.z3.q: What do I say when the Prophet ﷺ is mentioned?
k.dhikr.z4.q: Which of these is among the words Allah loves most?
m.welcome.s: A new beginning and a clean page
m.welcome.todo: Today, say from your heart: “All praise is for Allah, who guided me to Islam.”
m.welcome.ahlan.p:
All praise is for Allah, who guided you to Islam. You have chosen to worship Allah alone, and you are now a brother or sister to every Muslim on earth.
Islam wipes away the sins that came before it, so today you begin with a clean page.
m.welcome.yusr.h: Take your religion step by step
m.welcome.yusr.p:
Islam is a religion of ease. You are not asked to learn everything in one day. Learn the most important things first, and act on what you have learned.
The deeds Allah loves most are those done regularly, even if they are small.
m.welcome.first.l:
Understand the meaning of the two testimonies of faith.
Learn wudu and the prayer.
Keep the five daily prayers at their times.
Find a nearby mosque and good Muslim company.
Ask people of knowledge about what you do not know, and never be shy to ask.
m.shahada.s: The key to Islam and what it means
m.shahada.todo: Memorise the testimony in Arabic and understand its meaning.
m.shahada.text.p:
«أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أن محمدًا رسول الله»
Ash-hadu an lā ilāha illa-llāh, wa ash-hadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu-llāh.
“I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”
A person enters Islam with these words, saying them with the tongue and believing them in the heart.
m.shahada.ilah.h: The meaning of «لا إله إلا الله»
m.shahada.ilah.p: It means: no one has the right to be worshipped except Allah. Prayer, supplication, sacrifice, reliance and every act of worship are for Allah alone: not for a prophet, an angel, a saint, a grave or an idol.
m.shahada.rasul.p:
It means: to believe what he told us, to obey what he commanded, to leave what he forbade, and to worship Allah the way he taught.
He ﷺ is the servant and Messenger of Allah: a human being who is not worshipped, and a messenger who is not denied.
m.shahada.isa.h: What about Jesus (ʿIsa), peace be upon him?
m.shahada.isa.p: A Muslim loves Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and believes in him: a noble messenger, born of the Virgin Mary by a miracle from Allah. He is the servant and messenger of Allah; he is not God and not the son of God.
m.iman.todo: Name the six pillars of faith from memory.
m.iman.six.p: Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, asked the Prophet ﷺ about faith (Iman), and he named six things:
m.iman.six.l:
Belief in Allah: He is the Lord and Creator, He alone deserves worship, and His are the most beautiful names and the highest attributes.
Belief in the angels: beings created from light, who obey Allah and never disobey Him.
Belief in the books: such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, and the last of them, the preserved Quran.
Belief in the messengers: from Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus to the last of them, Muhammad ﷺ.
Belief in the Last Day: resurrection after death, the reckoning, Paradise and Hell.
Belief in the divine decree (Qadar), its good and its bad: everything happens by Allah's knowledge and will.
m.iman.allah.h: Knowing my Lord by His names
m.iman.allah.p: The more you know Allah, the more you love Him. Get to know His most beautiful names and their meanings: the Most Merciful, the Forgiving, the All-Hearing, the Near.
m.iman.qadar.h: Faith brings peace to the heart
m.iman.qadar.p: A believer knows that what has reached him was never going to miss him. So he is grateful in times of ease, patient in times of hardship, and never despairs of the mercy of Allah.
m.islam.todo: Read the next two steps (purification and prayer) this week.
m.islam.five.l:
The two testimonies: to testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
The prayer: five prayers each day and night.
Zakah: a fixed share of the wealth of the rich, given to the poor.
Fasting Ramadan: one month each year.
Hajj: the pilgrimage, once in a lifetime for those who are able.
m.islam.order.p: After the testimony, the first thing to begin with is the prayer: it is your connection with your Lord five times every day. Zakah, fasting and Hajj have their own times and conditions, and you will learn them when their time comes.
m.tahara.todo: Make wudu now, step by step, with this page in front of you.
m.tahara.ghusl.p:
It is prescribed for the one who enters Islam to take a full bath (ghusl). Ghusl means to intend it in your heart, then wash your whole body with water, rinsing the mouth and the nose as well.
Ghusl is also required after sexual intercourse or the release of semen, and for a woman when her menstrual or post-natal bleeding ends.
m.tahara.wudu.p: Prayer is not valid without wudu. This is how it is done:
m.tahara.wudu.l:
Intend wudu in your heart and say: «بسم الله» (Bismillāh).
Wash your hands three times.
Rinse your mouth and your nose three times.
Wash your face three times.
Wash your arms up to the elbows three times, the right and then the left.
Wipe your whole head once, and wipe your ears.
Wash your feet up to the ankles three times, the right and then the left.
m.tahara.breaks.p:
Wudu is broken by several things, among them: passing urine, stool or wind, deep sleep, and loss of consciousness. If any of these happens, make wudu again before you pray.
Washing each part once is enough; three times is better.
m.tahara.clean.h: A clean body, clothes and place
m.tahara.clean.p: After using the toilet, clean yourself with water. Pray in clean clothes and in a clean place.
m.times.t: The five prayers and their times
m.times.s: Your daily appointments with your Lord
m.times.todo: Set your city in the prayer times and turn on the alerts.
m.times.five.p: Allah has made five prayers obligatory for every Muslim each day and night. Each has its time and its number of rakʿahs (units):
m.times.five.l:
Fajr: two rakʿahs, from dawn until sunrise.
Dhuhr: four rakʿahs, after the sun passes its highest point.
Asr: four rakʿahs, in the late afternoon before sunset.
Maghrib: three rakʿahs, just after sunset.
Isha: four rakʿahs, after the red glow has left the horizon.
m.times.shurut.l:
The time of the prayer has begun.
You have wudu.
Your body, clothes and place are clean.
You are properly covered.
You face the qiblah (the direction of the Kaʿbah in Makkah).
m.times.jumua.p: On Friday, men pray the Friday prayer (Jumuʿah) in the mosque in place of Dhuhr: a sermon, then two rakʿahs with the imam.
m.times.miss.p: If you sleep through a prayer or forget it, pray it as soon as you remember. Never give up the prayer, whatever your shortcomings: it is the first thing that brings you back to Allah.
m.pray.todo: Pray the next prayer with this page in front of you.
m.pray.raka.l:
Stand facing the qiblah and intend the prayer in your heart.
Raise your hands and say: «الله أكبر» (Allāhu akbar: “Allah is the Greatest”).
Place your right hand over your left on your chest. Recite Surah al-Fatihah, then a short surah such as al-Ikhlas.
Say «الله أكبر» and bow (rukūʿ): back level, hands on your knees. Say three times: «سبحان ربي العظيم» (Subḥāna rabbiya-l-ʿaẓīm: “Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great”).
Rise from bowing saying: «سمع الله لمن حمده» (Samiʿa-llāhu liman ḥamidah). When you are standing straight, say: «ربنا ولك الحمد» (Rabbanā wa laka-l-ḥamd: “Our Lord, to You belongs all praise”).
Say «الله أكبر» and prostrate (sujūd) on seven parts: the forehead with the nose, both palms, both knees and the toes of both feet. Say three times: «سبحان ربي الأعلى» (Subḥāna rabbiya-l-aʿlā: “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High”).
Say «الله أكبر» and sit. Say: «ربِّ اغفر لي» (Rabbi-ghfir lī: “My Lord, forgive me”).
Say «الله أكبر» and prostrate a second time, like the first. This completes one rakʿah.
m.pray.rest.l:
Stand for the second rakʿah and do in it as you did in the first.
After the second prostration of the second rakʿah, sit and recite the tashahhud.
If the prayer has two rakʿahs (Fajr): continue with the blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then say the salam.
If it has three or four: stand after the first tashahhud and complete the remaining rakʿahs, reciting only al-Fatihah in each, then sit for the final tashahhud.
In the final sitting, recite the tashahhud, then the blessings on the Prophet ﷺ.
Turn your head to the right and say: «السلام عليكم ورحمة الله» (As-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatu-llāh), then to the left and say the same.
m.pray.new.h: If I have not memorised al-Fatihah yet
m.pray.new.p:
Do not delay the prayer until you have memorised it. Pray now, and while standing say what the Prophet ﷺ taught a man who could not yet learn any of the Quran: «سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله» (Subḥāna-llāh, wa-l-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illa-llāh, wa-llāhu akbar, wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh).
Work on memorising al-Fatihah soon, and pray in congregation at the mosque when you can: following the imam teaches you the prayer.
m.pray.women.p: A woman prays just as a man prays. She does not pray during her menstrual or post-natal bleeding, and she does not make up the prayers of those days.
m.quran.s: The words of Allah to you
m.quran.todo: Today, read the translation of the meanings of Surah al-Fatihah.
m.quran.what.p: The Quran is the speech of Allah. He revealed it to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Arabic and has protected it from any change. In it are guidance, healing and peace of heart.
m.quran.meaning.h: Read its meanings in your language
m.quran.meaning.p: Every day, read some of the translation of the meanings of the Quran in your language, even one page. A translation explains the meaning; the Quran itself is the Arabic text.
m.quran.learn.h: Learn to read it in Arabic
m.quran.learn.p: Learn the Arabic letters, then learn to read little by little. Whoever reads the Quran while finding it difficult has two rewards.
m.quran.hifz.p: Begin by memorising Surah al-Fatihah, then the short surahs: al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas. Repeat each verse with the reciter until it stays.
m.worship.s: Acts of worship with their seasons
m.worship.todo: Check the Hijri calendar to see how far away Ramadan is.
m.worship.sawm.p:
In the month of Ramadan a Muslim refrains from food, drink and marital relations from dawn until sunset, in obedience to Allah.
The sick and the traveller may break the fast and make it up later; a menstruating woman does not fast and makes it up later. If Ramadan comes while you are new to Islam, fast as much as you can and ask people of knowledge about anything that is unclear.
m.worship.zakah.p: Whoever owns wealth above a set minimum (the nisab) for a full lunar year gives one fortieth of it (2.5%) to the poor and needy. If your wealth is below the nisab, no zakah is due from you, and voluntary charity is always open to you.
m.worship.hajj.p: The pilgrimage to the House of Allah in Makkah is obligatory once in a lifetime for whoever is able, in health and in means.
m.halal.todo: Choose one habit to give up for the sake of Allah, starting today.
m.halal.asl.p: Allah has made all good things lawful for us, and has forbidden a few things because they harm us. Food, drink, clothing and dealings are lawful in principle, except what the texts have forbidden.
m.halal.food.p: Forbidden are: pork, the meat of animals that died without being slaughtered, blood, what was sacrificed to other than Allah, wine and every intoxicant, and drugs.
m.halal.kabair.p: The greatest is associating others with Allah (shirk). Then: magic and going to fortune-tellers, murder, sexual relations outside marriage, interest (riba), theft, gambling, mistreating parents, lying and backbiting.
m.halal.tawba.h: If you fall into a sin
m.halal.tawba.p:
Every human being makes mistakes. If you sin, ask Allah for forgiveness and turn back to Him. Do not despair of His mercy, and do not abandon your prayer because of a sin.
If you have an old habit that is forbidden, leave it for the sake of Allah, ask Him for help, and seek support from your brothers and sisters.
m.people.t: My family and the people around me
m.people.s: Your character is the best invitation
m.people.todo: Do a kindness for someone in your family today.
m.people.family.p:
Your Islam makes you kinder and more dutiful to your parents and family. Be good to them, visit them, help them and be patient with them. Only do not obey them if they tell you to disobey Allah.
Your good character with them says more than many words.
m.people.suhba.h: Good company and a nearby mosque
m.people.suhba.p: A person is influenced by the company he keeps. Look for a nearby mosque or Islamic centre, and get to know good Muslims who will support you and teach you.
m.people.sabr.p: Some people may find your Islam strange, or hurt you with a word. Answer harm with good. Do not argue about what you have not yet learned; simply say: “I do not know, I will ask.”
m.people.name.h: Do I have to change my name?
m.people.name.p: You do not have to change your name unless its meaning goes against Islam. For anything unclear in your personal life, ask a scholar you trust.
m.thabat.s: Day after day, until you meet Allah
m.thabat.todo: Today, in your prostration, ask Allah to keep you firm on His religion.
m.thabat.iman.p: Faith increases with obedience and decreases with sin. If you feel your energy fading, do not worry: renew your faith with prayer, the Quran, the remembrance of Allah and the company of good people.
m.thabat.dua.p: The Prophet ﷺ often used to supplicate: «يا مقلّب القلوب ثبّت قلبي على دينك» (Yā muqalliba-l-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ʿalā dīnik: “O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion”).
m.thabat.ilm.p: Seek knowledge from trustworthy sources and from its people. Each day read one hadith from the Forty Hadith of an-Nawawi and one page of the translation of the meanings of the Quran.
m.thabat.waswas.p: Whispers and questions may cross the heart. Seek refuge in Allah from Satan, say «آمنت بالله» (Āmantu billāh: “I believe in Allah”), and ask people of knowledge about what troubles you: asking is the cure.
m.thabat.daily.p: Use the “My day” page every day: begin with the essentials, then add little by little. A little that lasts is better than a lot that stops.

ui.kidsIntro: Short questions and easy answers, with evidence from the Quran and the Sunnah. Read, then test yourself and collect the stars!
ui.parentsText:
Read the question with the child and let them answer before seeing the answer. One unit per sitting is enough, repeated over the following days.
Connect each point to daily life: wudu at wudu time, eating manners at the table. Your example speaks louder than words.
The units go from belief to worship, then manners and remembrance, and suit children from about five years old together with their parents.
